## Case studies

- [Onboarding Funnel Redesign](/work/onboarding-funnel-redesign): Witzeal Technologies (real-money gaming), Product Manager. Day-7 retention was ~12%, and only 12% of new users played a game on their first day (D0): an activation problem, diagnosed through the onboarding funnel and OTP/API success and failure rates and delivery time. Five changes: simplified signup and login, email ID fetched automatically, OTP auto-read, first 3 games free (₹5 entry × 3 = ₹15 per user, against a ₹20 minimum first deposit; designed as a bridge toward first deposit, aiming for at least 5 game plays) and a live gameplay tutorial. In a 3-week controlled rollout (30% control, 70% treatment, about 50K users): D0 gameplay 12% → 33%; Day-7 retention 12.2% in control vs. 25.4% in treatment, +13.2 percentage points; positive direction into M0. The five changes shipped together, so individual contributions can't be isolated.
- [Adaptive Assignment Engine](/work/adaptive-assignment-engine): Edfora, Senior Product Manager. A fixed practice sequence was the wrong difficulty for many learners. Options weighed: learner choice, rule-based difficulty bands, ability estimation. Chosen: adaptive practice on a 3PL Item Response Theory (IRT) model that estimates each learner's ability (θ) and selects question difficulty to match. Across a 2-year academic-cycle dataset, assignment completion was 18% under the static learning path and 45% after the adaptive system was introduced (+27 percentage points); concurrent changes aren't on record, so the increase isn't attributed to the adaptive system alone.
- Baazi Games, PokerBaazi (real-money poker): optimized for D7 liquidity and player survival rather than only D0 ARPPU or raw server latency. Contextual matchmaking on historical wallet size and skill band reduced new players' exposure to inappropriate high-stakes tables; client-side polling only for active seat counts and static table metadata on edge CDN cache. Peak server latency under 60 ms, a lower D1 bankruptcy rate for new users, and net revenue growth alongside higher D30 retention.
- Baazi Games, FanBlaze (fantasy sports), a feature sunset: live in-app football scores were built to reduce context switching and lift contest participation. Fewer than 6% of active match-day users used the module; sessions grew ~2 minutes with no meaningful uplift in mid-match contest joins, lineup changes or re-deposits. Users already followed scores elsewhere, fantasy intent was mostly pre-match, and the sports API added cost without matching value. The feature was sunset and effort moved to starting-XI notifications, injury alerts and head-to-head stats.
- [AI Learner Diagnostic](/work/ai-learner-diagnostic): Independent portfolio prototype, not shipped at any employer and with no real users, production adoption or model results. Shows the rules vs. model split, grounding, failure modes and fallbacks, evaluation rubric, confidence UX and teacher override.

## Other documented outcomes

- Edfora: quiz and gamification layer, designed around teachers who found early prototypes "too game-y": DAU up ~12–15%, average session time up ~15%.
- Edfora: real-time engagement dashboards for faculty replaced a monthly spreadsheet pull: student retention up ~8–12%. Learning and engagement products reached 100K+ learners.
- Witzeal: a ~10% week-over-week GMV growth trajectory sustained over 11 months, alongside an experimentation roadmap across pricing and reward loops (not attributed to testing alone). Bonus allocation moved from flat tiers to expected ROI per segment (new, high-value, low-value, dormant/at-risk), optimizing incremental NGR per rupee of bonus spend: bonus spend down ~20% with retention held. Segmented lifecycle messaging: long-term retention stabilized at 48%.
- Baazi Games (PokerBaazi, Lagai Khai, FanBlaze): 20+ A/B tests, core funnel conversion up ~15%; behavioral segmentation, session duration up ~35% and retention up ~25%; rules-based fraud detection, fraud losses down ~18%.
- PwC India, Program & Release Manager: release process for a web application deployed to 150+ Fortune companies.
- Direct Create, Android Developer (2014–2018), not a product management role: sole Android developer; built the app from scratch and proposed one app with role selection for makers, buyers and designers instead of separate apps. Platform scale: 400+ maker shops and 100+ designers.
